# Plan: local deploy — render a whole system's manifests for a local cluster

> Revision 3. Revision 1 was reviewed against the codebase (verdict:
> rework); revision 2 resolved its five required items and was re-reviewed
> (verdict: approve-with-changes). This revision applies the re-review's
> five amendments: the catalog carrier (was silently dropped by
> `rawSpec`), the FetchLibrary test seams on `LocalOptions`, the pinned
> image-reference shape, values layering, and the pinnable predicate.

## The problem

The testing ladder has a gap at the top:

| Level | Scope | External systems |
|---|---|---|
| unit | one block | mocked in-process |
| integration | the pipeline in one component | mocked/stubbed |
| host | components together | mocked or in-memory |
| **local deploy** | **everything, deployed on a local cluster** | **real protocol, fake peer** |

Today nothing produces deployable manifests for a local cluster. The GitOps
machinery (`deploy init`, `deploy pin`, `deploy sync`) targets customer
environments through ArgoCD and is deliberately kubectl-free. A developer
who wants to run the full system locally — Dapr sidecars, pub/sub, bindings,
CronJob cadence and all — has to hand-write manifests.

The experience we want:

```
intropy int local <system> | kubectl apply -f -
```

One command, manifests on stdout, nothing written except one small state
file.

## The boundary

Three owners, no overlap:

| Owner | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| k3s setup scripts | The cluster, Dapr installation, and the fixture servers (sftp, smb, http stub) — **always installed**, at stable addresses with conventional dev credentials |
| intropy-templates repo | A `local` overlay on `deploy-host` / `deploy-component`, including the **closed fixture catalog**: one Dapr binding Component per fixture type, pointing at the conventional cluster addresses |
| this CLI | Reads the topology, asks one question per connector, renders into a temp dir, builds, streams YAML to stdout |

Consequences of "fixtures are always installed":

- The render is **unconditional**. The CLI never emits fixture servers at
  all, so there is no "include the sftp server only if some connector chose
  sftp" logic.
- Switching a connector's fidelity level (`file` → `sftp`) is a one-line
  edit in the state file and a re-apply. The cluster never changes.
- The CLI knows nothing about k3s. The emitted manifests are generic and
  would apply to any cluster with Dapr and the fixtures installed.

The fixture catalog is **closed**: `sftp`, `smb`, `http`, `file`. A system
needing something exotic hand-writes that Component in its own repo until
the pattern proves common enough to promote into the catalog (a template
PR, not a CLI release).

## The one coupling

The fixture contract — namespace, service names, ports, credentials — is
shared between the k3s scripts (which install the servers) and the
template's `local` overlay (which renders bindings pointing at them). One
doc, referenced from both repos. This is the only coupling between the two.

Conventions (initial proposal, finalized in that doc):

- namespace `fixtures`
- `sftp.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:22`, user/pass `intropy`/`intropy`
- `smb.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:445`
- `http.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:8080` (wiremock-style stub)

## The verb: `int local` — decided

Review finding 2 required deciding the verb in AGENTS.md terms instead of
deferring it. Decision: **`local`**, a new verb under `int`.

The AGENTS.md taxonomy rule: "New verbs need a reason that the set above
cannot express, and the reason goes in this file with the verb, not in a
commit message." The reason, to be added to the taxonomy with the verb:

> **`local`** renders a system's deployable manifests for the local
> development cluster to stdout, for piping to kubectl. `create` scaffolds
> project source on disk; `init` scaffolds a GitOps tree and pushes a
> branch. Neither emits a render to a stream, and both the GitOps `deploy`
> family is excluded by its own contract ("all through the GitOps
> repository and ArgoCD, never kubectl" — `deploy.go`).

Why not the alternatives:

- `int show <system> --manifests`: the command prompts, writes workspace
  state, and renders backing configuration — more than "prints the details
  of exactly one thing". `show` stays honest.
- A `deploy` subcommand: excluded by `deploy`'s documented contract, and
  by the parent command's design note that no component name may be
  shadowed by a subcommand.
- `int create local <system>`: collides with the template positional arg.
- `deploy-local` (rev 1's name): a hyphenated compound unlike every
  existing verb; nothing in the taxonomy licenses compounds.

## The local facts model — no GitOps repo involved

Review findings 3 and 4: `deploy init`'s facts all derive from a GitOps
checkout (`openSession`, `deploy.yaml`, `resolveInitDomain`). None of that
exists in this flow. This section specifies what replaces `newInitFacts`
— the plan's largest addition over rev 1.

`localFacts` (new, in `internal/deploy/local.go`):

| initFacts field | Source in `deploy init` | Source in `localFacts` |
|---|---|---|
| `Domain` | GitOps tree / workspace layout / `--domain` | **Omitted from staged paths entirely** (see below) |
| `System` | topology / `--system` | Same: topology record, `--system` override |
| `Environments` | `selectEnvironments(deploy.yaml)` | Constant: `["local"]` |
| `Registry` | `deploy.yaml` | Constant `"dev"` — placeholder only; every Deployment image is set by the CLI's kustomize `images[]` override (see `--image`), so the rendered registry is never pulled from |
| `AppNamespace` | `deploy.yaml` argocd section | Empty — ArgoCD facts have no local meaning |
| `Platform` | `deploy.yaml` platform section | Constants: provider `kubernetes`, pubsub `redis`, secretStore `kubernetes` — matching what the k3s scripts install |
| `Model` / `Scaffolds` / `Selected` | topology + scaffold walk | Same — unchanged reuse of `newInitModel`, `matchScaffolds`, `selectComponents` |

### Staged layout: flat, no domain segment

`deploy init` stages into `domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/` because
staged paths must be repo-relative for the commit. `int local` has no repo,
so the staging tree is flat:

```
<tmp>/
  kustomization.yaml          <- written by the CLI (below)
  host/                       <- deploy-host rendered once, env=local
    overlays/local/...
  <component>/                <- deploy-component per component
    overlays/local/...
```

`componentRelPath` is not reused; a `localRelPath(system, component)` =
`<component>` keeps paths stable without inventing a domain. (The system
segment is dropped too: the temp root already holds exactly one system.)

### The `.gitops` reserved map

Templates read `{{ .gitops.* }}` (reserved.go). For a local render the CLI
synthesizes:

```go
map[string]any{
    "domain":             "",          // no domain in a local render
    "system":             f.System,
    "component":          component,
    "env":                "local",
    "host":               HostDirName,
    "registry":           "dev",
    "argocdAppNamespace": "",
    "environments":       []string{"local"},
    "platform": map[string]any{
        "provider":    "kubernetes",
        "pubsub":      "redis",
        "secretStore": "kubernetes",
    },
}
```

Contract with the templates repo (stated in the fixture-contract doc): the
`local` overlay's skeleton files must not reference `.gitops` fields that
are empty locally — `argocdAppNamespace`, `domain`, `registry` outside base
image refs. Base files (rendered identically across envs per
`mergeRendered`) may reference `registry` freely because the CLI overrides
every image at build time.

### The root kustomization — CLI-written

Review finding 3: `deploy init` never builds the staging root (ArgoCD
builds each overlay separately), so nothing renders a root kustomization.
`int local` needs exactly one build, so the CLI writes it after rendering:

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: <--namespace value, default: system name>
resources:
  - host/overlays/local
  - <component>/overlays/local
  # ... one per selected component
images:
  - name: <image name as rendered by the component template>
    newName: <component>
    newTag: dev
  # ... one per pinnable component
```

- `namespace:` sets the target namespace on every resource — this is how
  `--namespace` is implemented; templates render namespace-agnostic.
- `images:` is how the conventional image tag is applied without the
  templates hardcoding it. **The rendered reference shape is pinned**
  (re-review finding 3): component templates render
  `image: <component>` — a bare name, no registry prefix, no tag. The
  fixture-contract doc states this, and the templates' unit tests assert
  it. The CLI therefore derives each `images[].name` as exactly the
  component name, and sets `newTag: dev` (no `newName`): the local image
  *is* `<component>:dev`, built and loaded by the scripts under that
  name. Pinning matters because kustomize image overrides match on the
  exact rendered name and **silently ignore unmatched entries** — a
  drifted convention would ship unoverridden images with no error. As a
  belt-and-braces check, `Local` parses the built output and errors if
  any Deployment image lacks a tag (catches template drift at render
  time rather than at pull time).
- **Pinnable predicate** (re-review finding 5): `images[]` gets one
  entry per selected component **except** the host — the same fact
  `requirePinnable` already encodes (`gitops.KindShared` has no image;
  init.go's HostDirName comment). The host renders no Deployment and no
  images entry.
- **`--image` grammar** (re-review finding 5): two forms, repeatable.
  `--image <component>=<name:tag>` overrides one component's entry
  (`newName` + `newTag`). `--image :<tag>` (a leading colon, no
  component) sets `newTag` on *every* pinnable component — the SemVer
  `-rc` flow (`--image :1.4.0-rc.3`). Any other shape is a usage error
  showing both forms.

### The build call

Review finding 1: the wrapper exists and the options struct must support
it. `internal/kustomize.Client.Build(ctx, dir)` (editor.go) runs
`kustomize build` and returns the stream; `plan.go` is the existing
caller. Accordingly:

```go
type LocalOptions struct {
    System      string
    SourceDir   string          // workspace root override (see below)
    Namespace   string
    Images      []string        // --image, repeatable (see below for the grammar)
    NoInput     bool
    TemplateVersion string      // same meaning as on deploy init
    TopologyFile string         // test seam, mirrors InitOptions.TopologyFile
    Runner      command.Runner  // for kustomize.Client; defaulted like InitOptions.applyDefaults

    // Library selection and fetch seams — mirrored from InitOptions
    // (init.go:104–114). GitHubBaseURL is how unit tests stub the
    // library fetch, exactly as init_test.go does; without it only the
    // INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR integration path could run. (Re-review
    // finding 2.)
    UserAgent     string
    Owner         string
    Repo          string
    GitHubBaseURL string
    HTTP          *http.Client

    Stdin       io.Reader
    Stdout      io.Writer
    Stderr      io.Writer
}

func Local(ctx context.Context, opts LocalOptions) error
```

`Runner` is required to construct `kustomize.Client`; `ctx` threads to
`Build`, `FetchLibrary`, and `runGraph`. The rendered YAML is written to
`opts.Stdout` — nothing else.

## The command

```
intropy int local <system> [--namespace <ns>] [--image <c>=<name:tag>]... [--template-version <tag>] [--no-input]
```

Behavior:

1. Resolve the workspace root (see below), run the host `graph` verb,
   decode via `topology.Decode` — same machinery as `deploy init`
   (`selectHost`, `discoverTopology`).
2. Load `.intropy/local.yaml`; prompt for unbound connectors; write the
   file back only if answers changed.
3. `template.FetchLibrary` (+ `defer lib.Close()`), render `deploy-host`
   once and `deploy-component` per component with env=`local` into
   `os.MkdirTemp`, `defer os.RemoveAll` on every exit path.
4. Write the root kustomization (above) into the staging root.
5. `kustomize.Client.Build(ctx, stagingRoot)`; write the multi-doc YAML
   to stdout.
6. Progress and hints to stderr only, house voice
   (`rendering order-extract for local`); follow-up hints in backticks on
   their own line.

`kustomize build` treats a temp dir identically to any other path; the
pipe to `kubectl apply -f -` sees only stdin. Two constraints, both
naturally satisfied:

- The staged tree is self-contained (kustomize's load restrictor refuses
  paths escaping the kustomization root) — the CLI renders everything into
  the temp root.
- No `helmCharts:` with remote repos in the templates — fixtures are
  pre-installed by the scripts, not rendered.

Flags:

- `--namespace` — target namespace in the emitted manifests (default: the
  system name). New flag, hand-written description.
- `--image` — repeatable image override (see root kustomization). New
  flag, hand-written description.
- `--template-version` — pins the template library release, same constant
  as `deploy init` (`flagUsageTemplateVer`). Review finding 8: rev 1
  omitted it; local renders must be able to pin the same library release
  the GitOps tree was scaffolded from.
- `--no-input` — fail instead of prompting (CI). Review finding 8: it
  already exists on two commands with two hand-written strings — this work
  introduces the shared `flagUsageNoInput` constant in `flagtext.go` and
  converts all three commands.
- No `--env` (always `local`), no `--output` (stdout is the manifest
  stream, period — review finding 8), no `--wait`, nothing that smells
  like kubectl.

Errors front-load what failed, remediation on a second line, per house
style — e.g. an unbound connector under `--no-input`:

```
connector erp-orders has no local binding in .intropy/local.yaml
run 'intropy int local <system>' interactively, or add it to the file
```

## What gets rendered — and what does not

Review finding 5: `deploy init`'s component template emits `component.yaml`
— repo metadata the rest of `deploy` reads, not a Kubernetes manifest.
Emitting it into a kubectl stream would be wrong.

The component template declares it in `spec.files`, so the mechanism is
already there: `int local` renders with a **narrowed file-rules filter**
that excludes `component.yaml` (and any future `*.md`/repo-metadata files
the contract doc enumerates). `renderOne` is reused with the filter
applied; the GitOps path is untouched. The exclusion list is part of the
fixture-contract doc so template authors know which files are repo-only.

ApplicationSet safety (the other half of finding 5): the guard lives in
the templates repo, not here. The ApplicationSet's cluster generator only
matches clusters registered in ArgoCD, so an `overlays/local/` directory
copied into a GitOps repo resolves to no cluster and generates no
Application. The templates-repo work item below includes verifying this
against the actual ApplicationSet template; this plan asserts no mechanism
of its own.

## Where the binding decision comes from

`internal/topology` is explicit: a `Connector` carries only its name,
external system, and directions. *"The deployed Dapr binding type, address,
and credentials are environment-owned deployment configuration, never part
of the record."* In production that decision lives in GitOps overlays. For
the local environment it lives nowhere — so `int local` is where it is
made.

The command asks **one question per connector** (not per component — the
topology's `UsedBy` already dedupes): "connector `erp-orders` (external
system `ERP`) — which binding?"

### The prompt: a new select prompter

Review finding 6: `template.AutoPrompter` is a missing-value text prompter;
no menu prompter exists. This work adds `template.SelectPrompter(stdin,
stderr, noInput)` to `internal/template/prompt.go` — shared, because a
catalog-driven menu is generally useful (skills flows are a likely second
caller). It presents a numbered menu, reads a number or name, and under
`--no-input` returns nil so the caller produces the two-line error above.

### The catalog: read from the fetched library, via a real Spec field

Review finding 6: a CLI-embedded catalog drifts from the templates repo
across releases. Decision: the catalog is **declared in the template
library** — a `fixtures` list in the `deploy-component` template's
`template.yaml`:

```yaml
spec:
  local:
    fixtures: [sftp, smb, http, file]
```

The CLI reads it from the fetched `lib` after `FetchLibrary`, so the
menu, the validation, and the rendered binding skeletons all come from
one release of one repo. Validation of `local.yaml` values happens
against the fetched catalog; an unknown value is a usage error naming
the valid ones. (Downgrade hazard noted in the first review is real but
bounded: the error message names exactly what the pinned library
supports, and `--template-version` is the escape hatch.)

**The carrier requires a manifest.go change** (re-review finding 1):
`Spec.UnmarshalYAML` decodes into a `rawSpec` listing exactly
`Parameters`, `Values`, `Files`, `Dependencies` — its own comment warns
"a field added to Spec alone is silently dropped", and yaml.v3 does not
error on unknown keys. A `spec.local` block would parse to nil with no
error and every `local.yaml` value would fail against an empty catalog.
So this work adds to `internal/template/manifest.go`:

- `Spec.Local *LocalSpec` where `LocalSpec{Fixtures []string}`, repeated
  in `rawSpec` (the whole point of the comment);
- validation in `validate()`: fixture names are non-empty, unique,
  lowercase path-safe tokens;
- a round-trip test asserting a `spec.local.fixtures` block survives
  load — the regression test for the silent-drop failure mode.

`template.yaml` files in the library without a `spec.local` block decode
to nil; the CLI treats a nil or empty catalog on `deploy-component` as a
hard error naming the library ref (a local overlay without a catalog is
a broken release, not a prompt with no choices).

### Workspace root and the state file

Review finding 6: "workspace root" was unstated. Definition: the directory
`selectHost` already searches — the host discovery root, i.e.
`--source-dir` when given, else the current directory, walked per
`ListScaffolds` (which skips `.intropy/` subtrees — no collision). The
state file is `<that root>/.intropy/local.yaml`, beside the host's
`.intropy/scaffold.json`.

Rules:

- A connector with a recorded choice is never re-prompted.
- A connector with no choice prompts (interactive) or errors under
  `--no-input`, listing what's missing.
- Values are validated against the fetched catalog.
- A connector removed from the topology leaves a stale entry; harmless,
  reported as a stderr note (`note: local.yaml binds crm, which the
  topology no longer declares`).
- The file is checked in: the whole team runs the same local topology, and
  CI runs non-interactively.

```yaml
connectors:
  erp-orders: sftp
  crm: http
```

## Values layering for the local render

Re-review finding 4. `int local` has **no `--values` and no `--set`** —
deliberately: every fact the templates need is derived (topology,
scaffold records, local constants, `local.yaml`), and an escape hatch
would let a local render diverge from the team's checked-in state in
ways nobody else can reproduce. Missing required template parameters
prompt through the existing `template.AutoPrompter`, exactly as
`resolveInitValues` drives it; under `--no-input` that prompter returns
nil and the parameter's absence surfaces as a resolve error. So the
`--no-input` failure surface is: unbound connectors (the two-line error
above) plus any template parameter with no default and no derived value.

## Templates work (intropy-templates repo, lands first)

- Add a `local` overlay to `deploy-host` and `deploy-component`. Content
  stays versioned with the templates it derives from, and the
  `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR` integration tests can cover it. A third
  standalone template was considered and rejected: two places describing
  the same Dapr components would drift.
- The `local` overlay carries the fixture catalog: one Dapr binding
  Component skeleton per fixture type, parameterized by connector name,
  pointing at the conventional fixture addresses. `spec.local.fixtures`
  declares the catalog (see above).
- Dev values, not `REPLACE-ME-*` placeholders: unlike `deploy init` (where
  a human fills placeholders before review), local output must apply
  cleanly on first run.
- Skeleton files must honor the `.gitops` emptiness contract (no
  `argocdAppNamespace`/`domain` references in the local overlay).
- `component.yaml` and other repo-metadata files must be declared in
  `spec.files` so the CLI's narrowed filter can exclude them — verify they
  already are; if any are unconditional, move them behind a rule.
- Verify the ApplicationSet's cluster generator cannot produce an
  Application for an `overlays/local/` directory (unregistered cluster ⇒
  no match). Document the result in the template's README.

## CLI implementation (this repo)

New files, mirroring existing seams:

- `internal/deploy/local.go` — `LocalOptions` / `Local` (above). Reuses
  `selectHost`, `discoverTopology`/`TopologyFile`, `newInitModel`,
  `selectComponents`, `template.FetchLibrary`, `renderOne` (with the
  narrowed filter and the local facts), `kustomize.Client.Build`. Adds
  `localFacts` + the root-kustomization writer.
- `internal/deploy/localconfig.go` — load/save/validate
  `.intropy/local.yaml` against the fetched catalog.
- `internal/template/prompt.go` — add `SelectPrompter`.
- `internal/template/manifest.go` — add `Spec.Local` / `LocalSpec`,
  repeat it in `rawSpec`, validate it, round-trip test (see "The
  catalog").
- `cmd/intropy/int_local.go` — cobra wiring.
- `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go` — add `flagUsageNoInput`; convert
  `int_create.go`, `deploy_init.go`, and the new command to it.

Tests (review finding 7 — mirror *both* existing seams):

- Unit: fixture templates served through the `GitHubBaseURL` fetch seam
  (as init_test.go:297 does) + **both** topology seams — package var
  `runGraph` (as init.go:39 establishes) and `LocalOptions.TopologyFile`
  — asserting rendered YAML per binding choice, root-kustomization
  contents (including the pinned image reference shape and the
  host-excluded images list), the untagged-image guard, prompt behavior,
  state-file round-trip, `--no-input` errors, stale-entry notes, and
  host discovery via `selectHost` the way init tests exercise it. Plus
  the manifest.go round-trip test for `spec.local.fixtures`.
- Integration: alongside `localtemplates_test.go`, under the same
  `//go:build integration` tag (rev 1 omitted it), gated on
  `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR` and run with `-count=1`. Renders with the real
  templates, parses the output as YAML, and validates with
  `kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -` — a second optional tool
  dependency, skipped via a `requireKubectl(t)` helper mirroring
  `requireKustomize`.

Docs:

- `docs/deploy-local.md` — the testing-ladder framing, the boundary table,
  the facts model, the state file, and a pointer to the fixture-contract
  doc. `Long:` stays ≤ 150 words; philosophy lives in the doc.
- `AGENTS.md` — add `local` to the verb taxonomy with the justification
  quoted in "The verb" above.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Building or loading container images.
- Installing anything — cluster, Dapr, fixtures are the scripts' job.
- Cluster introspection: the command never checks whether the cluster
  exists, Dapr is installed, or fixtures are reachable. It renders;
  kubectl applies; a missing cluster fails at apply time with kubectl's
  own error.
- User-defined fixture types (closed catalog).
- Pushing anything, anywhere: no git writes, no branches, no PRs. The only
  file written is `.intropy/local.yaml`.

## Order of work

1. Fixture-contract doc (scripts repo) — names, ports, credentials, the
   `.gitops` emptiness contract, the repo-metadata exclusion list, the
   `image: <component>` convention.
2. `local` overlay + fixture catalog + `spec.local.fixtures`
   (intropy-templates repo) — the CLI work is mostly plumbing against
   this. Includes the ApplicationSet verification.
3. `internal/template/manifest.go` `Spec.Local` +
   `internal/template/prompt.go` `SelectPrompter` + `flagtext.go`
   constant — small, unblocks the rest.
4. `internal/deploy/local.go` + `localconfig.go` + cobra wiring, unit
   tests against fixture templates.
5. Integration test against real templates.
6. `docs/deploy-local.md`, `AGENTS.md` taxonomy entry.

package main

import (
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli/internal/deploy"
	"github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli/internal/template"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

// deploy init scaffolds a system's kustomize tree into the GitOps
// repository. Everything non-trivial — topology discovery, rendering,
// staging, classification, push — lives in internal/deploy.Init; this file
// is flag plumbing and the call.
type initFlags struct {
	domain          string
	system          string
	envs            []string
	templateVersion string
	templateRepo    string
	values          []string
	sets            []string
	noInput         bool
	plan            bool
	force           bool
	gitopsRepo      string
	output          string
}

var initFlagValues = initFlags{output: deploy.OutputPlain}

var deployInitCmd = &cobra.Command{
	Use:   "init [component...]",
	Short: "Scaffold a system's manifests into the GitOps repository",
	Long: "Generate the kustomize tree a system needs in the GitOps repository, from the topology its host " +
		"declares.\n\n" +
		"Facts the CLI cannot derive — connection strings, hosts, credentials, cron schedules — are emitted as " +
		"REPLACE-ME-<HINT> placeholders and listed when the run finishes. Image tags are not in that list: " +
		"`intropy deploy` pins digests, and scaffolding never pins one.\n\n" +
		"--domain places the system in the tree. Note this differs from every other deploy subcommand, where " +
		"--domain narrows a search: here it is a destination. It is rarely needed — the domain comes from where " +
		"the system already sits, or from the workspace's domains/<domain>/<system>/ layout. A workspace with " +
		"several systems needs --system to pick one.\n\n" +
		"The run pushes deploy-init/<domain>-<system> for review, never the default branch: a tree of " +
		"placeholders would be picked up by the ApplicationSet immediately. Re-running is additive; a file that " +
		"already differs is reported and left alone unless --force is given, and --force still refuses an " +
		"overlay that pins a digest. --plan writes nothing and does not touch git.\n\n" +
		"See docs/deploy-init.md for the layout rationale and the Dapr ownership model.",
	Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
	RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
		if err := validateOutputFlag(initFlagValues.output, deploy.OutputPlain, deploy.OutputJSON); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		sets, err := template.ParseSets(initFlagValues.sets)
		if err != nil {
			return newUsageErrorf("%v", err)
		}

		owner, repo, err := resolveTemplateRepo(initFlagValues.templateRepo)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
		defer cancel()

		return deploy.Init(ctx, deploy.InitOptions{
			Components:      args,
			Domain:          initFlagValues.domain,
			System:          initFlagValues.system,
			Environments:    initFlagValues.envs,
			TemplateVersion: initFlagValues.templateVersion,
			Files:           initFlagValues.values,
			SetValues:       sets,
			NoInput:         initFlagValues.noInput,
			PlanOnly:        initFlagValues.plan,
			Force:           initFlagValues.force,
			GitopsRepo:      initFlagValues.gitopsRepo,
			OutputFormat:    initFlagValues.output,
			Color:           useColor(cmd),
			UserAgent:       "intropy-cli/" + version,
			CliVersion:      version,
			Stdin:           cmd.InOrStdin(),
			Stdout:          cmd.OutOrStdout(),
			Stderr:          cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
			Owner:           owner,
			Repo:            repo,
		})
	},
}

func init() {
	f := deployInitCmd.Flags()
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.domain, "domain", "", flagUsageInitDomain)
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.system, "system", "", flagUsageInitSystem)
	f.StringArrayVar(&initFlagValues.envs, "environments", nil, "environments to create overlays for (repeatable; default: every environment in deploy.yaml)")
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.templateVersion, "template-version", "", flagUsageTemplateVer)
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.templateRepo, "template-repo", "", flagUsageTemplateRepo)
	f.StringArrayVarP(&initFlagValues.values, "values", "f", nil, "values file (repeatable; - reads one document from stdin)")
	f.StringArrayVarP(&initFlagValues.sets, "set", "s", nil, "set a template value as key=value (repeatable)")
	f.BoolVar(&initFlagValues.noInput, "no-input", false, "never prompt; fail if a required value is missing")
	f.BoolVar(&initFlagValues.plan, "plan", false, "report what would be written without writing it or touching git")
	f.BoolVar(&initFlagValues.force, "force", false, "overwrite files that already differ (refused for an overlay that pins a digest)")
	f.StringVar(&initFlagValues.gitopsRepo, "gitops-repo", "", flagUsageGitopsRepo)
	f.StringVarP(&initFlagValues.output, "output", "o", deploy.OutputPlain, flagUsageOutput)

	deployCmd.AddCommand(deployInitCmd)
}

	Use:   "local <system>",
	Short: "Render a system's manifests for the local development cluster",
	Long: "Render deployable manifests for the local development cluster to stdout, for piping to kubectl: " +
		"`intropy int local <system> | kubectl apply -f -`.\n\n" +
		"The topology comes from the system host, exactly as deploy init reads it. Each connector needs a fixture " +
		"binding; the command asks once per connector and records the answers in .intropy/local.yaml at the " +
		"workspace root, which is checked in so the team renders the same thing. The catalog of fixtures comes " +
		"from the fetched template library release.\n\n" +
		"Every component image is rendered as <component>:dev — the tag the local build scripts load images " +
		"under. --image overrides that: --image <component>=<name:tag> for one component, --image :<tag> for all " +
		"of them.\n\n" +
		"The command never inspects the cluster and writes nothing but the state file; a missing cluster fails " +
		"at apply time with kubectl's own error. See docs/deploy-local.md for the boundary between this command, " +
		"the k3s scripts and the template overlays.",
	Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),

		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
		defer cancel()

			Images:          intLocalFlags.images,
			NoInput:         intLocalFlags.noInput,

			Repo:            repo,
			Stdin:           cmd.InOrStdin(),
			Stdout:          cmd.OutOrStdout(),
			Stderr:          cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
		})
	},
}

# int local — deploy the whole system on a local cluster

The testing ladder has a gap at the top, and this command fills it:

| Level | Scope | External systems |
|---|---|---|
| unit | one block | mocked in-process |
| integration | the pipeline in one component | mocked/stubbed |
| host | components together | mocked or in-memory |
| **local deploy** | **everything, deployed on a local cluster** | **real protocol, fake peer** |

```
intropy int local <system> | kubectl apply -f -
```

One command, manifests on stdout, nothing written except one small state
file.

## The boundary

Three owners, no overlap:

| Owner | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| k3s setup scripts | The cluster, Dapr, and the fixture servers (sftp, smb, http stub) — **always installed**, at stable addresses with conventional dev credentials |
| intropy-templates repo | A `local` overlay on `deploy-host` / `deploy-component`, including the **closed fixture catalog**: one Dapr binding Component per fixture type, pointing at the conventional cluster addresses |
| this CLI | Reads the topology, asks one question per connector, renders into a temp dir, builds, streams YAML to stdout |

Because fixtures are always installed, the render is **unconditional** — the
CLI never emits fixture servers, and switching a connector's binding
(`file` → `sftp`) is a one-line edit in the state file and a re-apply. The
emitted manifests are generic: they would apply to any cluster with Dapr and
the fixtures installed.

The fixture catalog is closed: `sftp`, `smb`, `http`, `file`. A system
needing something exotic hand-writes that Component in its own repo until
the pattern earns a place in the catalog (a template PR, not a CLI release).

The fixture contract — namespace, service names, ports, credentials — is
shared between the k3s scripts and the templates' `local` overlay, and
documented once in the scripts repo. It also pins two conventions this
command depends on:

- Component templates render `image: <component>` — a bare name, no registry
  prefix, no tag. The CLI's root kustomization overrides every one to
  `<component>:dev`, and kustomize silently ignores an override that matches
  nothing, so the guard described below exists.
- The local overlay's skeletons never reference the `.gitops` fields that
  are empty in a local render (`domain`, `argocdAppNamespace`).

## The facts model

`deploy init` derives its facts from a GitOps checkout. A local render has
no repository, so the facts are constants of the local cluster the scripts
install:

| Fact | Local source |
|---|---|
| environments | always `["local"]` |
| registry | `"dev"` — a placeholder; every image is overridden at build time |
| platform | provider `kubernetes`, pubsub `redis`, secretStore `kubernetes` |
| domain / ArgoCD app namespace | empty — no local meaning |
| model, scaffolds, selection | the same topology walk as `deploy init` |

The staging tree is flat — `host/`, one directory per component — because
the temp root already holds exactly one system and no commit needs a
repo-relative path.

## The state file

A topology connector carries only its name, external system and directions;
the binding type is environment-owned deployment configuration. For the
local environment that decision lives in `.intropy/local.yaml` at the
workspace root:

```yaml
connectors:
  erp-orders: sftp
  crm: http
```

The command asks one question per unbound connector — a menu from the
fetched library's `spec.local.fixtures` catalog — and writes the file back
only when an answer changed. The file is **checked in**: the whole team runs
the same local topology, and CI runs non-interactively with `--no-input`,
which fails with a two-line error naming what's missing. A connector the
topology no longer declares leaves a stale entry; harmless, and reported as
a stderr note.

Values are validated against the fetched catalog, so the menu, the
validation and the rendered skeletons always come from one release of one
repo. `--template-version` pins that release, exactly as on `deploy init`;
a library without a catalog is a hard error naming the ref.

## Images

Every component image renders as `<component>:dev` — the tag the local build
scripts load images under. The host has no image and gets no `images[]`
entry, the same fact `deploy pin` encodes. Overrides:

- `--image <component>=<name:tag>` — one component
- `--image :<tag>` — every component, the release-candidate flow
  (`--image :1.4.0-rc.3`)

After the build the CLI parses the output and fails if any Deployment image
lacks a tag: kustomize overrides match on the exact rendered name and
silently ignore misses, so a drifted convention would otherwise ship
unoverridden images with no error until pull time.

## What is deliberately not here

- No building or loading of container images.
- No installing anything — cluster, Dapr and fixtures are the scripts' job.
- No cluster introspection: the command renders, kubectl applies, and a
  missing cluster fails at apply time with kubectl's own error.
- No `--values`, no `--set`: every fact is derived, and an escape hatch
  would let one render diverge from the team's checked-in state.
- No git writes, no branches, no pushes. The only file written is
  `.intropy/local.yaml`.
